subject: Climate & Environment
title: Heart Disease from Dirty Air
description: One-minute skill: Heart Disease from Dirty Air.

hook.text: Air pollution doesn't just damage lungs. It is a leading cause of heart attacks and strokes.

buildup.text: Fine particles enter the bloodstream through the lungs and cause inflammation in arteries.

discovery.text: Chronic exposure thickens artery walls and promotes plaque buildup — the same process as high cholesterol.

twist.text: Studies show heart attack rates spike on high-pollution days, even in otherwise healthy people.

climax.text: Air pollution contributes to more cardiovascular deaths than smoking in some countries.

quiz.question: How does air pollution affect the cardiovascular system?

details.summary: Air pollution is a major but underrecognized cause of cardiovascular disease. Fine particles enter the bloodstream and trigger inflammation, blood clotting, and arterial plaque buildup, increasing the risk of heart attacks, strokes, and heart failure.
details.whyItMatters: Heart disease, not lung disease, accounts for the majority of air pollution deaths. This surprises most people and underscores why clean air is a cardiovascular priority.
takeaways: PM2.5 causes more cardiovascular deaths than respiratory deaths
Particles trigger systemic inflammation and accelerate atherosclerosis
Even short-term pollution spikes increase heart attack risk within hours

faq.question: How does breathing polluted air cause a heart attack?
faq.answer: Inhaled fine particles trigger lung inflammation that spills into the bloodstream, activating clotting factors and destabilizing arterial plaque. A pollution spike can provoke a heart attack in vulnerable individuals within hours.

faq.question: How many cardiovascular deaths does air pollution cause?
faq.answer: Air pollution contributes to an estimated 4 to 5 million cardiovascular deaths annually worldwide. Heart disease and stroke together account for more air-pollution deaths than all respiratory conditions combined.
